items.en: Vaculug has released the latest generation of its VMS Mobile App – VMS Pro Max – which is now available to download on the Apple App Store and Google Play Store. Developed over three years, VMS Pro Max combines “a completely redesigned user interface with AI-enhanced software and significant technology upgrades to make commercial fleet management faster, smarter and more efficient”.

After a winter of Florida sunshine, nature walks, and weekend camping trips, heading back to New York brings a different kind of checklist. Alongside closing up your seasonal home and packing outdoor gear, you need to decide how your car will return. Planning that step before your final week helps you enjoy the remaining days outside without squeezing every errand into departure morning.
Work Backward From Your Return Date

Start by identifying when you need to be home and when you can realistically release the vehicle in Florida. Those dates may differ, especially if you still need the car for airport transportation, grocery runs, or one last trail outing.

Navi Auto Transport’s guide to shipping a car from Florida to New York identifies March through May as the peak northbound snowbird period. If your return falls within that window, begin comparing arrangements before your schedule becomes inflexible. Request a quote using your actual locations, vehicle details, and available pickup dates.

Ask how the pickup window relates to estimated delivery, and arrange transportation for any days without the car. Keep your first weekend plans at home flexible until you know when the vehicle will arrive.
Sort Outdoor Gear Before Packing the Car

A winter’s worth of day hikes can leave the trunk full of boots, trekking poles, folding chairs, and half-forgotten supplies. Empty everything out before deciding what travels with you, what stays behind, and what needs a separate arrangement.

Clean and dry muddy footwear, tents, and damp clothing before packing. Remove leftover food and check under seats for items from earlier outings. Ask the transporter about its personal-belongings policy rather than assuming the car can serve as a moving container.

Flag camping fuel, propane cylinders, and similar supplies when discussing restrictions, and arrange an appropriate alternative instead of leaving them inside. Keep medication, identification, house keys, and any gear you need immediately in your own travel luggage.
Give the Vehicle a Clear Handoff

Wash the exterior enough to make its condition easy to see, then take dated photographs from several angles. Include existing scratches or dents and review the pickup condition report with the driver. Save copies where you can find them during travel.
Before pickup, confirm:
- The carrier’s fuel-level and preparation instructions.
- Whether roof boxes, bike racks, or other accessories need removal.
- Which keys the driver needs and how to handle the alarm.
- The agreed meeting location and primary contact number.
Tell the coordinator about vehicle modifications or operating problems in advance. Details that seem minor during everyday driving may matter when arranging loading.
Prepare for Delivery in New York

Check whether a large transporter can access your destination. If a nearby meeting point is required, plan how you will reach it and who will accompany you if needed. Confirm the process for authorizing another person to receive the car if you cannot attend.

At delivery, compare the vehicle with the pickup record and document any differences before completing the handoff paperwork. Allow time for that inspection rather than scheduling it between tightly timed appointments.
Leave Room for Your Next Outing

Once the car is home, unpack and reorganize your outdoor kit before planning another trail day. Check the conditions and access information for your intended destination, and make sure the equipment you packed for Florida suits the next trip. A little preparation at both ends makes the transition from winter away to weekends back home easier to manage.
